title: Introduction
description: The ideas behind Minerva, how to read the component pages, and the conventions shared by every component.

tokens.title: Token-driven
tokens.text: colors, radii and shadows come from CSS custom properties, so every component follows the active theme, including your own.

accessible.title: Accessible by default
accessible.text: components render native, semantic elements, support the keyboard, show a visible focus ring and expose aria-label where a visible label may be missing.

predictable.title: Predictable APIs
predictable.text: the same prop names (variant, size, shape, disabled, loading...) mean the same thing across components.

small.title: Small and composable
small.text: components do one thing and accept className and style, so they are easy to combine with your own layout and styles.

reading.title: How to read the component pages
reading.text: Every component page follows the same structure:
reading.import: the exact import statement of the component. The global stylesheet is not repeated there: it is imported once, in your app entry (see Installation).
reading.examples: live demos covering each feature. Use "Show code" to see the complete source; every demo is self-contained and can be copied as is. Demos report what happened on the page with Minerva's own components (a toast, a dialog or an inline result), never with browser alerts or the console.
reading.api: tables generated from the component's TypeScript types, with the type, the default value and a description of every prop.

controlled.title: Controlled and uncontrolled
controlled.text: Form components can manage their own state (pass defaultChecked / defaultValue, or nothing) or be controlled (pass checked / value together with onChange). Do not switch between the two modes during a component's lifetime.

passthrough.title: className and style
passthrough.text: Components accept className (and usually style) on their root element. Components that wrap a native element, such as Button, also forward the native attributes (type, name, data-*, aria-*...).

aria.title: Accessible names
aria.text: When a control has no visible text (an icon button, a search button, a close icon...), give it an accessible name with the aria-label prop. It is passed through to the interactive element.

browsers.title: Browser support
browsers.text: Minerva targets current evergreen browsers: Chrome and Edge 111+, Firefox 113+ and Safari 16.2+. The theme relies on CSS custom properties and color-mix(); Internet Explorer is not supported. Server-side rendering works, the theme is applied on the client once React mounts.

contributing.title: Contributing
contributing.text: Minerva is open source under the MIT license. Bug reports, ideas and pull requests are welcome on GitHub:
